text: Bad comments make me hesitate really
Very accommodating and friendly staffs. I am satisfied with the treatment. 😄 …

It's located on the 2nd floor of Home Place in Thonglor 13. Booking appointments is very convenient as you can email them online in Japanese and schedule appointments. I was surprised that the Thai receptionist spoke excellent Japanese, including her accent. Everything I wanted to say was clearly communicated.

I went because a silver filling had fallen out, and the dentist was very thorough. As is common in Thailand, they don't provide the same detailed explanations as in Japan, which might make Japanese people feel uneasy, but overall, I had a good impression.

The initial consultation fee was 600B, filling was 1,800B, and tartar removal was 2,000B.

I had a dental filling done by two doctors (probably the male director and a female doctor), and they did it very well. Their techniques are excellent. You can use LINE in Japanese, and the receptionist is a Thai who speaks fluent Japanese. At first I was a bit worried about going to a dentist in a foreign country, but they are faster and probably better than in Japan.

It's easy to get confused, but this is Bangkok. Not Japan. And yet, there's no language barrier at all. This environment is truly wonderful. It feels even more so when you come from another city. Some people say there's no detailed explanation or the prices are high, but if they think it's too expensive here, they should go back to Japan and get treatment. And those who say there's no explanation, did you ask questions properly? Even if you ask in Japanese, you'll get a proper explanation and answer in Japanese. I think patients should also be careful. The director, as well as the female receptionist, have excellent Japanese language skills, which are particularly noteworthy. I was impressed by the truly personable director, female doctor, and receptionist.

I previously went here for tartar removal and cleaning.
However, the treatment was incredibly painful, and when it was over my teeth were covered in blood. In the end, it seemed like they had scraped away everything except the teeth around my back teeth, and some of the flesh was scraped away like a really bad mouth ulcer.
Due to the composition of my teeth, I am prone to cavities, and since I was little I have been going to them for cleanings and cavity treatment 3-4 times a year. However, this is the first time I have ever experienced such poor treatment at a dentist.
During the treatment, the dentist told me to relax, but it was just too painful to put up with the tartar removal and cleaning.
I will never use their services again.

Three years ago, I was diagnosed with a cavity at a Japanese dentist's office and had a filling put in, but it recently came out. I felt pain while flossing, so I went to see a dentist.

During the examination, they couldn't find anything, and the X-ray showed nothing resembling a cavity. There wasn't much of an explanation, which left me a little uneasy...

The initial consultation fee was 600 baht, the examination fee was 300 baht, and the X-ray was 700 baht, for a total of 1600 baht.

This was my first time being examined at a Thai dental clinic.

The receptionist spoke Japanese and helped me interpret.

I was suddenly hit with a toothache and went to a dentist overseas for the first time.
The initial consultation fee was 600 baht, and although the X-ray showed nothing particularly abnormal, the dentist suggested that if it hurt, they could just have the tooth extracted. I'm not sure if this is a common occurrence in Thailand, but it made me feel a little uneasy.
The medicine they prescribed was also available over the counter in Thailand, so I think it was a bit expensive.
There was an interpreter, so I was able to communicate in Japanese without any problems.

A few years ago, I had a dental plaque removed by a female dentist, but she accidentally drilled into an unrelated tooth, leaving a small hole in my tooth. When I pointed this out to her, she denied it, and when I asked how much the treatment would cost, she told me it would cost 34,000 baht to cover it with ceramic. I couldn't leave it as it was, and although I wasn't happy, I had no choice but to ask for treatment. She immediately took an impression and created two large holes in my tooth, so there was no evidence left. I got increasingly angry when I got home and canceled any future treatment. It was the worst.

They offer excellent Japanese language support. They're skilled at treating cavities (around 2000 THB per tooth). Wisdom tooth extractions (around 8000 THB per tooth) are also performed without any infection or other complications. It's expensive, but their skills are undeniable.
